summary: A small, symmetrical two-story rectangular/symmetric Minecraft house with a stepped slab roof. Visible materials include stone brick blocks for the lower walls and foundation, smooth stone slabs for the layered roof, wooden planks as a mid-level horizontal band and accents, glass panes for continuous windows, glowstone lighting blocks at corners, and stone brick slabs/stone slabs for trims. The footprint is a centered cross-like rectangle (main rectangle with a centered front bay and rear narrower extension) visible from top-down.

shape.overall_form: rectangular main volume with a centered protruding front bay and a narrower rear extension; stacked two main levels with layered slab roof
shape.symmetry: bilateral symmetry across front-back axis (mirrored left-right)

materials.name: wood
materials.role: mid-level horizontal band and small accents (planks)

elements: continuous horizontal windows (glass panes) on both visible floors
central front entrance bay with small landing/step
layered stepped slab roof (multiple concentric slab layers)
glowstone corner lights on middle level
wooden plank band between first and second levels
rebuild_hints: Lay a stonebrick rectangular base ~9x13 with a centered front 3-block protrusion and a centered 1-block rear extension (see top-down cross-like layout).
Build two stacked volumes: first-floor height ~3 blocks, second-floor height ~3 blocks; separate floors with a horizontal wood plank band across the facade.
Place continuous 3-4 block long horizontal glass pane windows on both floors centered on the facade, with glowstone at the second-floor window corners.
Construct roof from concentric offset layers of stone slabs (each layer inset from the one below) culminating in a small slab cap.
Use stone slabs and possibly wood slabs for the small entrance steps/ledge.
uncertainties: Exact block types for wooden elements (could be oak planks or another wood) are not certain.
Some trim pieces may be stonebrick stairs or slabs instead of full blocks; slab vs stair usage uncertain.
Top-down footprint shows a cruciform-ish shape; exact rear extension depth and internal partitioning are uncertain.
Presence and location of an interior floor/ceiling and internal stairs are not visible.
